fact: Le Soleil reports that the communications and telecoms minister launched deployment of free Starlink satellite kits in Kolda on 10 April 2026, a government programme to connect 1 million Senegalese free by end 2026 in remote zones, with a first lot of 200 of 1,000 kits ready.

Agence Ecofin reports that in February 2026 Senegal's authorities announced they had negotiated the purchase of 5,000 Starlink kits at a preferential rate, aiming to help connect up to one million Senegalese, notably in remote areas, under the New Deal technologique.

Le Soleil reports that the government's New Deal Technologique provided for the State to buy 5,000 Starlink kits at a preferential rate to serve white zones, community wifi networks and the connection of schools and local authorities.
The State announced the acquisition of 5,000 satellite kits for white zones (uncovered areas), per columnist Isaac Sissokho, secretary-general at the digital ministry.

fact: The universal service fund FDSUT's Projet d'Acces Universel plans 4G coverage of 1,550 universal-service localities over 2024-2028, with partnership agreements with operators and site deployment still listed as next steps.

Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko said a universal connectivity programme is under way to serve white zones, with the aim of free internet access for more than one million citizens, notably in rural and isolated areas.
